Assume countable choice. Take a balanced multipointed diagram for one oriented knot in $S^3$ with the splitting, compression disks and cyclic marking convention of the balanced pointed-data definition, without assuming its admissibility. Write $A_i$ and $B_i$ for the components of the complements of the two attaching systems, numbered so that $w_i,z_i\in A_i$ and $w_i,z_{i+1}\in B_i$, with cyclic indices, $1\le i\le k$.

Every integral domain $P$ whose boundary is an integral sum of full attaching curves has an integral representation
$$P=\sum_{i=1}^k a_iA_i+\sum_{i=1}^k b_iB_i.$$
If $n_{w_i}(P)=0$ for every $i$, then $b_i=-a_i$ and
$$n_{z_i}(P)=a_i-a_{i-1},\qquad \sum_i n_{z_i}(P)=0.$$
Such a domain is zero if all its $z$ multiplicities vanish. Consequently every nonzero such domain has both a positive and a negative region coefficient: the diagram is admissible in the precise periodic-domain sense of that Definition. In particular every balanced knot diagram appearing in a valid knot-preserving multipointed move sequence in $S^3$ is admissible, without a further winding modification. This assertion does not construct the move sequence or analytic moduli spaces.

Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed Riemann surface with two systems $\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta$ of $m\ge1$ pairwise disjoint curves in each system, with transverse finite opposite-system intersections. Let $L_\alpha,L_\beta$ be their product tori in $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m\Sigma$. Choose one interior point $a_R$ in each complementary region and exact product charts about every intersection generator, disjoint from the diagonal and every divisor $E_{a_R}$. Consider smooth finite-energy holomorphic strips with uniform generator ends, for paths $J_t$ equal to the standard symmetric-product structure near the diagonal and every $E_{a_R}$. The perturbation paths may have different interior values; the surface, attaching systems, region points and product generator charts are fixed.

For such a strip set $D(u)=\sum_R n_{a_R}(u)[R]$, with the actual integer divisor multiplicities. If $u$ and $v$ have the same ordered generator ends, then
$$\partial(D(u)-D(v))=\sum_i A_i\alpha_i+\sum_j B_j\beta_j$$
for integers $A_i,B_j$, as a full oriented curve-chain identity. Thus $D(u)-D(v)$ is a periodic domain in the full-curve sense, not merely a homologically periodic chain. If both ends of $u$ are the same generator, its own domain is periodic.

This assertion is proved from actual finite ordered lifts and local degree identities, without an index formula, a Chern pairing or a surjectivity assertion about arbitrary region domains. It makes no claim that every periodic domain or continuous Whitney class has a holomorphic representative.

Let $\Sigma$ be a closed Riemann surface, $m\ge1$, and $p\in\Sigma$. In the complex symmetric product $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ let $E_p=\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$. Let $L_0,L_1\subset X$ be compact submanifolds disjoint from $E_p$. Suppose $J_t$ agrees with the fixed complex structure of $X$ on one neighborhood of $E_p$ for every $t\in[0,1]$. Let $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ be a smooth solution of $\partial_\tau u+J_t(u)\partial_tu=0$, with boundary on $L_0,L_1$ and uniform limits as $\tau\to\pm\infty$ at points of $L_0\cap L_1$.

The intersections of $u$ with $E_p$ are a finite collection of interior points, each with positive integral local intersection multiplicity. Their sum is nonnegative, and it is zero exactly when $u$ avoids $E_p$. In pointed Heegaard data, with $L_0,L_1$ the product tori and $p$ any marked point, this proves nonnegativity of the domain multiplicity $n_p(u)$ whenever it is defined by intersection with $E_p$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed connected Riemann surface, $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ with its standard complex structure, and $m\ge1$. For $a\in\Sigma$ put $E_a=\{a\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$. This is a smooth complex hypersurface, including at repeated tuples. The universal incidence hypersurface $\mathcal E=\{(a,D):D\in E_a\}\subset\Sigma\times X$ carries a smooth complex divisor line bundle with its canonical section, whose zero set is $\mathcal E$ with multiplicity one.

For a smooth map $v:S\to X$, where $S$ is an oriented sphere or a closed disk, define $n_a(v)$ as the degree of the pullback point-divisor line bundle; for a disk use the canonical section to trivialize it on the boundary, and require $v(\partial S)\cap E_a=\varnothing$. The proof constructs this integer by elementary frame winding. It is defined even when a sphere lies wholly in $E_a$.

For a sphere, $n_a(v)$ is independent of $a$ on all of $\Sigma$. For a disk whose boundary tuples have all entries in a finite union of curves $\Gamma\subset\Sigma$, it is independent of $a$ on each connected component of $\Sigma\setminus\Gamma$. If $v^{-1}(E_a)$ is finite and the map is holomorphic on a neighborhood of every one of these points, then
$$n_a(v)=\sum_{z\in v^{-1}(E_a)}\operatorname{ord}_z(F_a\circ v)\ge0,$$
where $F_a$ is any local holomorphic defining function of the smooth hypersurface $E_a$. Each term is a positive integer. Thus the degree agrees with proper holomorphic intersection multiplicity, while divisor containment is handled by its degree definition and actual point movement rather than an unsupported proper-intersection assumption.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(\Sigma,j)$ be a closed Riemann surface with positive area form $\eta$, and put $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$, $m\ge1$, with its induced complex structure $J_0$. Let $q:\Sigma^m\to X$ be the quotient, $\Delta\subset X$ its repeated-point locus, and $\Omega=\sum_{l=1}^m\operatorname{pr}_l^*\eta$. Off $\Delta$ the permutation-invariant form $\Omega$ descends to a smooth form $\omega$ on $X\setminus\Delta$. Equip $X$ with any smooth Riemannian metric $g$.

Let $L_\alpha,L_\beta$ be product tori formed from two finite systems of pairwise disjoint attaching curves, with transverse intersections between the systems. Suppose a smooth path $J_t$ agrees with $J_0$ on a neighborhood $V$ of $\Delta$ and tames $\omega$ on $X\setminus V$. Let $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ be a smooth $J_t$-holomorphic strip, with boundary on these tori, finite $g$-Dirichlet energy, and uniform limits at both ends to intersection generators. For each complementary region $R$ of the attaching curves write $n_R(u)$ for the signed intersection multiplicity of $u$ with $\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$ at a generic $p\in R$.

There is a constant $C$ depending only on the fixed geometric data and the path, independent of $u$, such that
$$E_g(u)=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R\times[0,1]}(|u_s|_g^2+|u_t|_g^2)\,dsdt\le C\sum_R n_R(u)\int_R\eta.$$
In particular energies of all such representatives with one fixed domain are uniformly bounded. The finite-energy hypothesis here is explicit; no assertion that arbitrary asymptotically convergent smooth solutions automatically have finite energy is included.

derivations.claim: If $m=h+k-1=0$, the symmetric product is a point and every strip is constant with zero marked multiplicities and zero energy, so the assertions hold directly. Assume henceforth $m>0$. For every full-curve periodic domain the representation [F1] gives $$\sum_{j=1}^k n_{w_j}(P)=\sum_i a_i+\sum_i b_i=\sum_{j=1}^k n_{z_j}(P).$$ Indeed each $A_i$ contains precisely one point from each marked set, and each $B_i$ does as well; the cyclic shift of the beta $z$ index permutes that sum. This is an evaluation of integral region chains at the actual points, including when several marks occupy one region. For two zero-$z$ strips with the same ends, [F2] makes $P=D(u)-D(v)$ periodic and its total $z$ coefficient zero. The displayed identity therefore makes their total $w$ coefficients equal. If any strip for that endpoint pair exists, this common integer $S_{xy}$ is nonnegative by [F3]. Otherwise use the convention in the Statement. [F1, F2, F3, given, construct, algebra]

Each individual $w$ coefficient of an actual strip is an integer between zero and $S_{xy}$ by [F3]. There are at most $(S_{xy}+1)^k$ such vectors, hence finitely many. If two strips with the same ends also have the same vector, their periodic difference from [F2] has every $w$ coefficient zero and every $z$ coefficient zero. The last conclusion in [F1] makes that difference zero, so their entire domains agree. This proves one domain per vector and finitely many domains per ordered endpoint pair, without selecting or realizing any merely formal domain. For a same-generator strip compare with the actual constant strip at that generator. Its zero marked domain makes $S_{xx}=0$ by step 1.1. Thus all $w$ coefficients of the given strip are zero, and its already zero $z$ coefficients and [F1]–[F2] make its entire domain zero. The estimate [F4] forces energy zero, and smoothness on the connected strip makes the map constant. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

The generator set is finite, since there are finitely many attaching-curve intersections and finitely many matching tuples. Steps 1.1–2.1 give a finite union of actual domain sets across its finitely many ordered pairs. For a fixed path the right sides $C\sum_R n_R\int_R\eta$ of [F4] consequently take only finitely many values; taking their maximum plus one bounds every actual strip energy. If there are no strips, use bound one. The same reasoning applies to a collection of paths with common geometry and one common energy constant $C$, because the periodic-domain comparison in [F2] compares those paths too. There is no selection over infinitely many classes or parameters: the finite possible vectors and the one-domain assertion suffice, and one may choose one actual witness from each nonempty finite-domain set using finite choice. No Fredholm index has entered this argument. [F2, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

For completeness the needed uniform $C$ is locally available. Choose one smaller diagonal neighborhood whose closure lies in the fixed integrable one. Off it, the background path has a positive minimum of $\omega(v,J_tv)$ on the compact parameterized unit-vector bundle; on the portion inside the integrable neighborhood this follows from the fixed product complex structure. A sufficiently small $C^0$ variation preserves half this minimum and a common bound on $|J_t|$, giving the uniform pointwise energy-to-area estimate there. On the integrable diagonal part the product metric and derivative of the fixed quotient map are unchanged. These are exactly the two bounds used in the actual proof [F4], so one constant works for all paths in that neighborhood. The stated finiteness and energy conclusions retain positive $w$ multiplicities wherever they actually occur. No genericity, domain-index identity or Floer comparison has been inferred. [F4, step 3.1, construct, algebra] ∎

Step 1.1 treats m0 directly; step 2.1 proves samegenerator totalw0, domain0 and actualenergy0.
